name: Kirya-Konzel
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Blench & Ndamsai, DRAFT Dictionary of Fali of Kirya (Kirya-Konzel), rogerblench.info PDF via the Internet Archive (read): tone section only, no word-stress statement
earlier_scan.note: only extant sketch describes tone; word stress never mentioned

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Anthony Ndamsai. 2007 [Glottolog dates it 2006]. A dictionary of Kirya and Konzəl in Northeastern Nigeria [Draft circulated for comment; printout Jos, 6 Dec 2007; running head 'Draft Dictionary of Fali of Kirya']. Cambridge/Jos: ms., 53 pp.
sources.note: Section 3 Phonology (pp. 8-10) = 3.1 Vowels, 3.2 Consonants, 3.3 Tones. Only prosodic statement is the tone paragraph (p. 10): two level tones H and L, rare downstep, rare rising/falling. The words 'stress', 'accent', 'prominence' do not occur anywhere in the 53 pages (a full-text search for stress/accent the text).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. Kirya opening page (index of his Kirya materials: dictionary, Bayreuth slides, offprint, 'Kirya trees', Meek extract, photo webshows).
sources.note: Confirms the complete inventory of Blench's Kirya materials; no further linguistic descriptions exist there beyond the two examined.
No phonology; supplied the URL of Blench's dictionary PDF.

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The phonology of Proto-Central Chadic: the reconstruction of the phonology and lexicon of Proto-Central Chadic, and the linguistic history of the Central Chadic languages. LOT 375. Utrecht: LOT. Section 6.5.6 Kirya-Konzel, pp. 170-171.
sources.note: Discusses only Kirya vowels, labialized/palatalized consonants and the retroflex [ɽ], drawing on Blench 2009; the reconstruction is stated to exclude 'tone or stress'. Nothing on Kirya stress.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2011. Change Request 2011-085: create [fkk] Kəryə-Konzəl (submitted by Zachariah Yoder, SIL; adopted 2012-02-03).
sources.note: Identity/classification only; cites Blench & Ndamsai 2007 and Yoder et al. (forthcoming) sociolinguistic survey. Nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Antony Ndamsai. 2009. An introduction to Kirya-Konzəl: A central Chadic language of Eastern Nigeria. In Eva Rothmaler (ed.), Topics in Chadic Linguistics V: Comparative and Descriptive Studies (Papers from the 4th Biennial International Colloquium on the Chadic Languages, Bayreuth, 30-31 Oct 2007), 75-85. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe. (author's offprint scan)
sources.note: Section 3 (3.1 Vowels, 3.2 Consonants, 3.3 Tones, pp. 79-81) reproduces the dictionary's phonology verbatim; 3.3 Tones gives the same two-tone statement. No mention of stress or accent (scanned a full-text search for stress/accent: no hits).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2007. 'Blench Chadic Bayreuth 2007' conference slides (PowerPoint HTML export).
sources.note: Slide text not recoverable from the Internet Archive (slide files 404); content is presumably the same as the 2009 paper, so unlikely to add a stress statement.

sources.citation: Meek, Charles K. 1931. Tribal Studies in Northern Nigeria, vol. 1, pp. 300-309 ('Fali of Kirya' section; extract posted by Blench). London: Kegan Paul, Trench, Trübner.
sources.note: Ethnographic notes plus a short wordlist; nothing on tone, stress or accent.

sources.citation: Yoder, Zachariah, Katarína Hannelová, Linus Otronyi & David van der Vloed. [2011?]. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Fali of Mubi in Adamawa State, Nigeria. SIL International (Electronic Survey Report series, number not verified).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only other primary work on the language besides Blench & Ndamsai; a sociolinguistic survey with wordlists, so a stress statement is unlikely, but it should be checked to close the record.

sources.citation: Kraft, Charles H. 1981. Chadic Wordlists, Vol. II (Biu-Mandara). Marburger Studien zur Afrika- und Asienkunde A/24. Berlin: Dietrich Reimer. Kirya list pp. 179ff.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Phonetically transcribed wordlist with tone marks; the introduction to the volume may state whether stress was noted in transcription. Blench calls its tones and phonemes unreliable.

sources.citation: Mohrlang, Roger. 1972. Higi Phonology. Studies in Nigerian Languages 2. Zaria: Institute of Linguistics / Centre for the Study of Nigerian Languages.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: held in print at Harvard (Tozzer Library, call number Microfiche L.SOC. 120.Tx. 8.5.12.1 (2)); ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library, call number Microfiche L.SOC. 120.Tx. 8.5.12.1 (2)
sources.note: The phonology of the closest relative (Higi = Kamwe [hig]); Blench & Ndamsai use it as their comparison baseline. Any stress statement there would be for Kamwe, NOT Kirya, and could only serve as family context.
